record.paper_title: Some results and open problems in research on low dimensional organic conductors
record.original_question: For Bechgaard salts modeled from the one-dimensional Hubbard Hamiltonian, what is the dependence of the electrical conductivity on band filling? Here band filling means the ratio of the number of electrons to the number of lattice sites, and experimentally it can be changed by doping with electron donors or acceptors. The open problem is to carry out the conductivity calculation and determine how conductivity varies as the filling changes, especially in relation to the thermodynamic behavior near half filling.

evidence.quote: An important characteristic of this model is the "band filling" which physically corresponds to the ratio of the number of electrons divided by the number of lattice sites.
It would be useful to perform a calculation of the conductivity, and check its behaviour as a function of the filling.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the one-dimensional Hubbard Hamiltonian on a chain of L sites,
   H = -t \sum_{i,\sigma} (c_{i,\sigma}^\dagger c_{i+1,\sigma} + h.c.) + U \sum_i n_{i,\uparrow} n_{i,\downarrow},
with hopping amplitude t > 0, on-site repulsion U > 0, fermionic operators c_{i,\sigma}, c_{i,\sigma}^\dagger, and number operators n_{i,\sigma} = c_{i,\sigma}^\dagger c_{i,\sigma}. Define the band filling n = N_e / L, where N_e is the total number of electrons.

Using the Kubo formula, the (temperature- and frequency-dependent) electrical conductivity \sigma(\omega, T; n, U/t) is determined by current-current correlation functions of the current operator
   J = -i t e \sum_{i,\sigma} (c_{i,\sigma}^\dagger c_{i+1,\sigma} - c_{i+1,\sigma}^\dagger c_{i,\sigma}).

Determine analytically (or to the extent possible) the dependence of the conductivity \sigma(\omega, T; n, U/t)—including the Drude weight, the regular part, and the dc limit—on the band filling n for 0 < n < 2 at fixed U/t. In particular, describe the qualitative and quantitative behaviour of \sigma as n approaches the half-filled point n = 1, and relate the resulting filling dependence to the thermodynamic properties (e.g., charge compressibility and spin/charge gaps obtained from the Bethe-ansatz solution) of the model in the vicinity of half filling.
artifact.status_search_result: The optical/Drude conductivity of the 1D Hubbard model has been studied extensively via Bethe-ansatz, bosonization, and numerical (DMRG, Bethe-ansatz-based) methods. Results exist for the Drude weight as a function of filling and U/t, and for the optical conductivity at and away from half filling, including dimerized/extended variants relevant to Bechgaard salts. A complete closed-form expression of the full conductivity as a function of filling, frequency, and temperature is, however, not available, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Optical conductivity of the one-dimensional dimerized Hubbard model at quarter filling
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates optical conductivity in the Mott insulating phase of the 1D extended Hubbard model with dimerization at quarter band filling.
status_evidence.claim: Filling-dependent optical conductivity has been computed in extended 1D Hubbard variants relevant to Bechgaard salts.

status_evidence.title: Deducing correlation parameters from optical conductivity in the Bechgaard salts
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical calculations of kinetic energy in extensions of the 1D Hubbard model, combined with f-sum rules, used to constrain conductivity in Bechgaard salts.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results connecting 1D Hubbard conductivity and filling to Bechgaard salt observations are available.
